Create / operator guide

CREATE: from an event name to a details page

Before you start: this is a developer-operated workflow, not an all-in-one creation UI. Reading this guide needs no sign-in. Running it requires source repository access, granted by the owner, plus the setup and data access below. Repository-file links may require that access.
On this page
  • 1. Prepare; choose rebuild or new event
  • 2. Turn the name into a registered candidate (manual)
  • 3. Screen coverage; stop if it cannot answer the question
  • 4. Build radar, terrain and optical layers
  • 5. Research stories/media, then make human selections
  • 6. Validate and open the actual details page

Minimum deliverable: this operator guide, using the existing Python pipeline and static site. There is no free-text event-name command or creation server/UI. The browser editor selects stories for an already-built event; a local/self-hosted creation UI is a stretch, not implemented. An event name starts research, not a guaranteed build: suitable NISAR coverage and an interpretable signal are prerequisites. A valid outcome is “not suitable yet”, with the reason recorded.

1. Prepare; choose rebuild or new event

Run commands from the repository root. First-time setup (Python 3.12):

python3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt

Use a free Earthdata Login bearer token in the environment variable EARTHDATA_TOKEN (set it privately in your shell; the pipeline reads the environment, not a .env file).

Viewing the committed site and searching CMR need no login. A cache-miss build needs the token, network access to ASF, Copernicus DEM on AWS and Element 84 Earth Search; the browser needs WebGL and access to the three.js CDN. Dependencies are in requirements.txt. Never put credentials, signed download URLs or raw HDF5 downloads in the repository.

  • Existing event: keep its registered slug and researched inputs. The supported worked example below is kumamoto-quake. You can skip new registration/research, but review coverage and outputs.
  • New event: do steps 2–6. A new name is not accepted until you register a structured candidate, check coverage, build the layers and supply researched, human-reviewed story inputs.
  • Builds overwrite generated files and update the shared index/credits. Preserve unrelated changes; run builds serially. Serving a page locally does not publish it or require a Git commit.
SLUG=kumamoto-quake  # existing worked recipe; replace with your registered slug for a new event

2. Turn the name into a registered candidate (manual)

Verify the exact event/year, onset date and affected footprint from original agency/news sources; record citations and uncertainty in research notes (see validation sources). Use the actual fire perimeter, debris corridor, flood area or vent, not just a nearby town's centroid. Choose a centre in decimal WGS84 latitude/longitude and a square window whose half-width is half_km in km. Include the whole footprint plus stable reference ground; start around 30–40 km for a large quake, 10–20 km for a local change, then inspect actual coverage.

Append an object to events in pipeline/candidates.json, keeping existing entries and a unique URL-safe slug. This is the existing example's schema, not a second entry:

{"slug":"kumamoto-quake", "name":"Kumamoto M6.8 earthquake, Japan",
 "kind":"quake", "lat":32.682, "lon":130.722, "date":"2026-07-28", "half_km":30}

Required: slug, name, kind, lat, lon, date, half_km. Use ISO YYYY-MM-DD; date: null is for ongoing subsidence, not an unknown event date. Supported kinds and actual selection rules:

Kind Product and selection in pipeline.build_event
quake, volcano, landslide GUNW: shortest pair with start < date <= end across all stacks; latest preceding pair on the same stack as baseline, if available.
flood, fire GCOV HH/HV: same stack, at least two pre-event passes; take up to three before, first one after (flood) or up to two (fire). Choose earliest post-event coverage.
subsidence (date: null) GUNW: consecutive shortest pairs from the earliest date on the largest stack; cumulative LOS fitted to a steady rate. Inspect gaps and retained pairs.

Optional fields: after_from (ISO date; delay GCOV post-event selection, e.g. until a fire's final scar), reach_km (documented volcanic run-out), note (GUNW page caveat; GCOV currently does not copy it). Do not copy newland: true to a new volcano: that extra GCOV analysis is Anak Krakatau-specific (fixed dates/projection/crop and a required stories file), not a generic new-land detector. Landslide thresholds are tuned to Himalayan monsoon valley floors; another setting needs validation, not just a changed name. Unknown kinds are not a supported extension point.

3. Screen coverage; stop if it cannot answer the question

.venv/bin/python -m pipeline.coverage

This searches public CMR for all registered candidates, writes site/data/coverage.json and prints rankings. Collections are NISAR_L2_GUNW_PROVISIONAL_V1 / NISAR_L2_GCOV_PROVISIONAL_V1 in pipeline/cmr.py. It tests the centre point, not full-window coverage or signal quality. Compare only one (track, frame, ascending/descending direction) stack. Check granule footprints in ASF Search and later check the built grid/masks cover your footprint.

Preview the builder's actual choices with public metadata only (no radar download):

.venv/bin/python - "$SLUG" <<'PY'
import sys
from pipeline import build_event as b

ev = b.candidates()[sys.argv[1]]
if ev["date"] is None:
    chosen = b.chain(ev)
elif ev["kind"] in b.BACKSCATTER:
    pre, post = b.pick_passes(ev)
    chosen = pre + post
else:
    across, baseline = b.pick_pairs(ev)
    if baseline is None:
        print("WARNING: no quiet baseline; coherence-drop evidence is unavailable")
    chosen = [g for g in (baseline, across) if g is not None]
for g in chosen:
    print(g.id, g.stack, g.start, g.end)
PY

A coverage score is only a screen: GCOV scoring wants two passes on each side, whereas the builder accepts two before/one after; scoring ignores after_from. Subsidence scoring counts a stack, not its continuous chain. The builder does not enforce a score or choose the cleanest signal. There is no CLI track/granule override; a different scientific selection requires a reviewed code change.

Stop/defer for no spanning pair, no adequate same-stack passes, an unusable chain, or a flood already drained before the first post-event pass. Keep the candidate and document why; do not add a fake live page. Recheck later for archive/product lag, or choose another event. CMR errors are not proof of absent coverage: resolve the service error and rerun. A missing baseline prevents the baseline comparison/coherence-drop story even if the across-event motion layer builds.

4. Build radar, terrain and optical layers

.venv/bin/python -m pipeline.build_event "$SLUG"
# Only when deliberately refreshing acquisitions, or after changing date/centre/extent/kind:
# .venv/bin/python -m pipeline.build_event "$SLUG" --refetch

First run reads HDF5 windows through HTTP ranges (not entire multi-GB granules); budget minutes and potentially substantial network traffic, especially for a chain. cache/<slug>.npz is reused by slug, not keyed by parameters. Use --refetch after scientific input changes. Only load trusted caches. A missing/expired Earthdata token or ASF access failure is an authentication blocker, not “no event”.

The build reprojects Copernicus GLO-30 terrain and Sentinel-2 L2A onto the radar grid. Optical windows are event −75 to −1 days / +1 to +45 days; for subsidence the anchor is chain end minus 60 days. Cloud-masked composites use up to six dates each. Draping uses after, then before to fill holes; GCOV also falls back to radar brightness. Without optical, ordinary GUNW can have no ground texture. Missing DEM tiles become zero: check that land has real terrain, not a silent download/coverage gap. STAC/network failures may abort the build; fix them rather than treating an incomplete folder as ready.

Outputs: site/events/<slug>/meta.json (grid, provenance, dates, stats, image credits), binary layers, images and ground texture when available. GUNW yields LOS/coherence and, with a baseline, coherence loss; GCOV yields backscatter change, not motion; subsidence yields fitted cumulative motion/rate. The build adds the slug to site/events/index.json automatically, but does not build stories. Inspect baseline versus event signal, valid area, cloud gaps and agreement with independent mapped extents. Low coherence is not proof of damage; explain mismatches in the page/story text, or stop. See ingest methods and limitations; event animation is interpolation, not a recording.

5. Research stories/media, then make human selections

For a new event create research/stories/<slug>.json manually. Use the Kumamoto source as the concrete schema example: top-level slug, boundary (one checked sentence), items (array). Every item needs a stable id, title, place, lat, lon, side, what_it_shows, image_url, page_url, credit, licence, date, confidence, notes. Use side = affected or unaffected only with evidence; confidence = high/medium/low. Verify source pages, event/year, location and rights yourself. Aim for a well-located hit/spared pair, not invented people, damage, sources or coordinates. An empty items array is a technical bootstrap, not a completed ground-story page. Approximate locations cannot prove opposite sides of a boundary.

Optional enrichment (not needed for a radar + researched-story page):

  • Media harvest requires a hand-written research/media/seeds/<slug>.json first; see seed schema, providers and outputs and the four existing seed files. It is not generated from an event name. .venv/bin/python -m pipeline.media "$SLUG" --only=commons,gdelt avoids Mapillary; the default harvest's Mapillary provider needs MAPILLARY_TOKEN. Harvest rewrites candidates and may geocode/update seeds; inspect failures and wrong matches. Its relevance/tiering is quake/subsidence- oriented, not a validated generic hazard search.
  • .venv/bin/python -m pipeline.establishing "$SLUG" finds optional Commons place photos; review research/establishing/<slug>.json and mark bad choices "rejected": true. These are labelled context, not pictures of the event. .venv/bin/python scripts/places.py "$SLUG" adds optional OSM labels.
.venv/bin/python -m pipeline.stories "$SLUG"
.venv/bin/python -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory site

The first command samples radar at researched points and creates site/events/<slug>/stories.json. It may fetch image previews; it also regenerates per-event CREDITS.md. Keep the server running in this terminal. Open http://localhost:8000/editor.html?e=kumamoto-quake (substitute your slug), select/ reject candidates, order and caption them, and download decisions into research/editorial/<slug>.json. Browser autosave alone never updates repository files. Decisions have boundary text plus items/media maps keyed by ID, with status, caption and order. In another terminal at the repo root, rerun .venv/bin/python -m pipeline.stories kumamoto-quake (or your slug) to apply them. The page falls back to non-rejected candidates marked unreviewed if no selected in-frame stories remain; do not mistake that for editorial approval.

Retain source URLs, creators, licences and modification notices. News images may become pixelated linked previews in the current pipeline; pixelation is not permission. If rights are unclear, use link-only text with image_url: null and no preview_file. Review harvested previews too. Add any new dataset/software/service attribution to the hand-maintained part of CREDITS.md; regenerate its marked per-event block with pipeline.stories or .venv/bin/python -m pipeline.credits, never by hand. Selected Mapillary URLs can expire; see editorial shipping checks.

6. Validate and open the actual details page

Worked example URL: http://localhost:8000/e/kumamoto-quake.html. After building or changing stories, run scripts/pages.py below to regenerate the static event pages and their titles/descriptions. It reads site/events/index.json, writes site/e/<slug>.html and makes site/index.html the Kumamoto landing page. Edit site/event.html, not those generated copies.

For a new event use http://localhost:8000/e/<slug>.html; the shared template also works at http://localhost:8000/event.html?e=<slug>. Do not open an events-directory URL or file://. The catalogue at events.html lists site/data/coverage.json and links built slugs from site/events/index.json to their static pages. A new event therefore needs the coverage refresh, a successful build and page generation. Neither JSON file is an editorial-readiness gate. Generated asset folders alone do not register a candidate.

.venv/bin/python scripts/pages.py
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_pipeline.py
.venv/bin/python -m pipeline.credits --check
# Optional macOS screenshot, with the server above still running and Chrome installed:
PORT=8000 sh scripts/shot.sh 'e/kumamoto-quake.html' /tmp/nisar-event.png

Before calling it ready, check the actual new slug, not just the example: metadata dates/extent/ provenance, every referenced layer/image, binary sizes (nx × ny bytes for u8, twice that for i16), working 3D/slider, in-frame pins, reviewed stories/media, source links/credits, caveats and catalogue link. Inspect the screenshot and browser console/network errors; automated tests do not establish scientific validity or rights. Changed grids also require resampling stories and refreshing optional media/places; existing media seeds' computed steps are cached in the seed JSON, not auto-invalidated. Optional lab/sideways-slip outputs are separate, not generated for arbitrary events by this recipe.

Verification and remaining limits (15 November 2026)

Checked source/CLI contracts, relative links and the committed Kumamoto fixture/asset sizes. Shell/JSON/ Python examples pass syntax checks; metadata preview ran with mocked CMR for all six kinds. All 11 pipeline tests and pipeline.credits --check passed. After the static-route update, all seven shell blocks passed syntax checking and the page generator reproduced the twelve committed event pages and landing page in memory. The public guide and existing Kumamoto page were browser-checked; that is not a new-event build. The full repository suite passed (27 Python + 10 presentation tests).

No authenticated fetch, rebuild, fresh new event or live coverage check was run. Credentials, network, scientific review and human research/editorial remain prerequisites. No all-in-one creator, automatic scientific quality gate or generic new-event smoke test exists; a creation server/UI remains stretch scope. See the presentation QA record for the browser checks and their limits.
